posts.name: Jeff V
posts.cooked:
I did not like it either, since I use FreeCAD regularly. However it is available as an AppImage and that works on F39.

I suspect that the maintainer for fedora did not want to update the app to work with python 3.12 and the upstream has not yet done so. This would mean that the requests for update should go to the upstream developers.

posts.cooked: How hard is it to become a volunteer for making the .rpm files? I really hate flatpak/snaps/appimages and I’m kinda interested to become a volunteer for making the .rpm for freecad, and also arduino which has also been gone for a while, but I’m really unsure I have enough technical skills for it…

posts.name: Avram
posts.cooked:
It’s not very difficult to become a package maintainer. The best way to gain skills is to do it and people are generally helpful.

For FreeCAD, you’d have to start with the F38 Branch and update it for the latest FreeCAD release. Once you get that working, it needs to be submitted for review and, once it passes review, you submit a ticket to fedora releng to unretire the package. There may be another step to take over the repo, or it may be that can be combined with unretiring.

### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing iss…ues ### Problem description Fedora nightly builds on COPR fail. However even after quick fix and attempting to build the package in copr myself in a private project, there still seem to be problems. The F38 build still fails, I need to examine further why, and the F39 build fails because of missing dependencies, probably because python-pyside2 is still non-existent on F39/F40 (that package fails for unrelated reasons to FreeCAD). posts.name: George N. White III
posts.cooked:
You might get a start on becoming a maintainer by investigating the nightly build failures, but I suspect the reliance on Python clashes with the need to support multiple Fedora versions. I use some Python apps that need older Python versions. Fedoras offers older Python, but some upstream devs are focusing on condo packages. I don’t know if a Fedora policy requires packages to use the current python version. I do know that Apple explicitly says Python apps should not rely on the Apple provided python.

You may want to discuss issues you find with upstream. If you can solve those failures the maintainer may find time to implement them or pass the task off to you.

I should mention that there is a growing list of more specialized 3D CAD packages targeting specific use-cases: architecture, 3D printing, solid objects, etc. This is where CAD developers may prefer focusing effort on AppImages (reaching more users with available resources while avoiding issues with differences in distro libraries and security mechanisms).

posts.name: David T
posts.cooked: Yeah. Flatpak is your only option especially for something like FreeCAD, unfortunately. The quality of FreeCAD has not been so good, not to mention the bikeshedding of the lead devs in the community. I wouldn’t expect it to be reinstated. It used to be a good FOSS project, but those days are gone.

posts.name: Ulysses A
posts.cooked:
I worked as a professional engineer for a while. I used the proprietary Kompas-3D on Windows machines and FreeCAD at home on Linux. FreeCAD has always been a pretty decent CAD program, but it had its issues. Like an awkward UI, crashes, and illogical behavior when building the model dependency graph. With the release of version 1.0 last year, and now 1.1, FreeCAD has made huge usability improvements. FreeCAD has become much, much better. If you’re saying it’s gotten worse, then I think you don’t use it.

It’s very strange that FreeCAD isn’t in the Fedora repositories. Especially considering FreeCAD is in copr. I use FreeCAD from a flatpak now, but I’d be happy if FreeCAD were in the Fedora repositories. Then I’d use the trusted Fedora flatpak.
